national.line: Wu-Tang Clan will perform at halftime of the Detroit Lions' Thanksgiving Day game against the Bears. Turkey and Wu-Tang, both bring the ruckus.

Hundreds of students at Howell High School in New Jersey collected over a quarter million pounds of food and covered their football field with donation bags for food banks last week. That's a touchdown for hunger.
Florida teachers Maren and David Douglass surprised a schoolgirl, whose bus stop is the end of their driveway, with a bench after she'd been sitting in the dirt. Now that's a front-row seat.
An elderly sailor who vanished with his dog during a trans-Pacific trip was rescued off the California coast. Best first mate ever.
An 85-year-old woman in a senior home brought down the house with a cover of Fleetwood Mac's "Landslide." Stevie Nicks may need to look over her shoulder.
A man known as "Unc" has strangers asking him to name their kittens, with names like Hersberry, O'dis and Nuffin. Nuffin wrong with that.
Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce dressed as each other for Halloween, while the Mahomes family went as Toy Story characters. Kansas City knows how to trick-or-treat.

pride.label: World Champion
pride.line: Victoria Moroski, 17, of Lake of the Ozarks, won gold in the under-18 Skim division at the World Wakesurf Championships in China in October, and Team USA won team gold. That's one way to make a wake.

pride.label: Life Saving Award
pride.line: A Missouri Cooperage worker collapsed from a cardiac event July 8, and on Oct. 26 eight people got Lebanon's Life Saving Award for saving him: coworker Tyler Blattel, Lt. Joe Gerber, firefighters Adam Moppin, Nick Davis and Paul Shomo, Capt. Terry Saltzman, paramedic Louis Corbeil and EMT Jeremy Vinson. Real heroes with great timing.

pride.label: Yellowjacket of the Week
pride.line: Ollie Sanders was named Lebanon High School's Yellowjacket of the Week, and the favorite moment was winning best colorguard at Carthage. Sounds like a flag-waving week.

pride.label: New Leader
pride.line: Lebanon Schools named Katie Cottongim its new Director of Communications. Now there's someone with plenty to say.

pride.label: Navy Scholarship
pride.line: Chapel Banner, a Bolivar High School senior, earned a four-year Navy ROTC scholarship, one of about 100 awarded nationwide this year through the early-selection path. Anchors aweigh.

pride.label: Apprenticeship Complete
pride.line: Julia Jones finished her Dental Assistant Registered Apprenticeship through the Bolivar clinic and the school district's BoMo Works program, and plans to become a dental hygienist. A career with a bright smile.

pride.label: Student Project
pride.line: Waynesville Career Center welding and manufacturing students, taught by Adam Rodden, built backdrop props for the Waynesville High School marching band and saved about $10,000 this fall. Now that's welded harmony.

pride.label: District Champs
pride.line: Bolivar softball won the district title with a 12-2 win over Aurora, then fell 16-5 to Southern Boone in the state quarterfinal in October. Next year, the bats come back.

local.line: Heritage Bank of the Ozarks won the Oct. 26 foreclosure sale for Lebanon's Ice Cream Factory property and is working with the city on its future. Here's hoping the next chapter is sweet.

Camden County Public Water Supply District No. 5 received a $223,000 interest-free loan from the Missouri Department of Natural Resources on Oct. 27 to plan and design drinking water upgrades. Nothing flows like savings.
Marshfield High School is bringing back its Marine Corps JROTC program after a four-year effort. Marshfield is marching again.
Lake Regional Clinic in Osage Beach added pediatric nurse practitioner Courtney Wood, who offers acute walk-in care, well-child visits and sports physicals. One less thing for parents to schedule.

music.line: Ella Langley loves Halloween, but drew the line at fans throwing candy onstage because it's a tripping hazard. Safety first, sugar second.
Morgan Wallen now has his own 24/7 SiriusXM channel, Morgan Wallen Radio, that he curates himself. Somebody finally gets the aux cord.
Morgan Wallen announced 2027 dates for his Sand In My Boots Festival and says he plans to make it even better. Hard to top, but he's trying.
Zach Top added new arena dates to his Cold Beer & Country Music Tour. More dates, more boots to stomp.
Lauren Alaina is playing "Stages," "All My Exes" and "Road Less Traveled" on the final stops of her tour, including Nashville's Ryman Auditorium. The Ryman gets the grand finale.
Parker McCollum says he wanted to quit country music right as his career was taking off, amid burnout. Good thing he stuck around.
Nick Jonas, Reba McEntire, Tim McGraw and more will perform at "Disney Celebrates America: Nashville's Star-Spangled Bash." Mickey's going country.
Randy Travis is playing "Forever and Ever, Amen" and "Three Wooden Crosses" at the final shows of his "More Life" tour. Forever and ever, in concert.
Garth Brooks' Double Live gets its first vinyl release on Nov. 6. Time to dust off the turntable.
Whisperin' Bill, the Grand Ole Opry's longest-serving member, turns 89. That's a whole lot of Opry nights.

weird.line: A Florida man called 911 thinking his Yukon SUV was stolen, but it had been repossessed before he'd made a single payment. Turns out the thief was the bank.
A college student unofficially broke the world record for fastest jet-powered drone, hitting 491 mph with an aircraft built in his dorm. Nothing says dorm life like a jet.
Texas firefighters rescued a raccoon whose head got stuck in a hole in a tree. Even the raccoon needed a hand.
A Florida man spent two years building a street-legal car from real aircraft parts to look like a WWII fighter. Please keep it out of the school pickup line.
An exhausted raccoon climbed aboard a kayak and napped for hours in the tackle box. Best fishing trip it never planned.
A snake poked its head out of a Kansas driver's dashboard air vent in the middle of a drive. Talk about a hot vent.
A man cooking chicken at an outdoor eatery found a snake hidden in a bag of charcoal. The special just got a little too spicy.
An 82-year-old Florida man has spent seven decades collecting magazines, photographs and celebrity memorabilia. His closet has stories.
A pink rock found in the Sahara turned out to be a 4.1-billion-year-old fragment of Mars. Somebody's lawn decoration just got upgraded.
A Wisconsin angler shattered a 75-year-old state smallmouth bass record with a 9.7-pound fish. That fish story is actually true.
A 19th-century custom box holding a perfume bottle, a garter and a revolver, with a dagger in the lid, sold at an estate sale for $39,999. Grandma's attic never had this.
A GraviTrax marble run built a bluebird mosaic in 16 minutes by releasing hundreds of pre-positioned colored marbles. Somebody's patience just earned its wings.
Dogs react to Halloween decorations in funny ways: some fear a nefarious intruder, some chase a black cat cutout, and one puppy wanted the bone of an artificial skeleton. Pup logic is undefeated.
Area 51 likely got its name from the numbering system used at the Nevada Test Site. The big secret was just a number.
Heidi Klum turned her own hand into her 2026 Halloween costume. She really did lend a hand.
Michigan just had its biggest pumpkin harvest this century. That's a lot of pie.
A motorcycle company founder rode 25 miles across a river for a Guinness World Record. Hope he packed a towel.
Matt Robertson won a record $1.25 million at the first-ever World Bass Enterprises "Champions" tournament. Now that's a big catch.
The interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS carries a chemical clue suggesting it formed 7 billion years ago. Older than your grandpa's jokes.
A Florida man jumped through a window to escape police. Not the exit most people use.

humor.line: It's a day to stop stressing over something you keep telling yourself you should do, like exercising or getting organized. The laundry has been excused.
Author Nancy Christie came up with it so you'd spend the hour gained when clocks fall back relaxing instead of working. Doing nothing has never sounded so productive.
McCormick, the spice company, created it in 2019 to kick off what it calls Cinnamon Season. Somebody in marketing deserves a cinnamon roll.
Nellie Verne Burt McPherson, president of a women's club in Bement, Illinois, thought it up in 1928 to thank her favorite author, Irving Bacheller. Fan mail, the original kind.
Calzone is Italian for "trousers," and it began in Naples as a street food for workers on the go. Pizza that came dressed for dinner.
In 1884, 25 nations met in Washington, D.C., to pick zero longitude: 22 voted for Greenwich, Haiti voted no, and France and Brazil abstained. Even the map needed a vote.
The word "vegan" was coined in November 1944, and Nov. 1 was picked because nobody knew the exact date. Somebody forgot to write it down.
The clams usually deep fried are the soft-shelled kind, nicknamed "clam bellies" or "steamers." Nobody asks which belly they're eating.

It honors radio and TV traffic departments on the anniversary of the first commercial radio broadcast, KDKA in Pittsburgh in 1920, which reported presidential election results. Thank a traffic director, they make the spots run.
Cookie Monster's early role on Sesame Street was undefined and he didn't even have a name until the second season. Me glad he got a name.
Deviled eggs also go by eggs mimosa, stuffed eggs and dressed eggs. Whatever you call them, they vanish at potlucks.
It's meant for kids learning shapes to look up, down and every which way and point out circles, but adults count too. Your steering wheel is fair game.
It falls on the birthday of John Montagu, the Earl of Sandwich, who legend says came up with the sandwich in 1762. Best career move: lending his name to lunch.
It's a day to use cliché phrases as much as possible, even though they're usually overused. At the end of the day, it is what it is.
You're supposed to give someone a dollar, whether a friend, a stranger or a charity. A dollar won't buy much, but it buys a smile.
Jellyfish are about 95 percent water, have no bones, and aren't even fish. So technically, wobbly water.
King Tut became pharaoh at nine years old, and his tomb was found by Howard Carter in 1922. Most nine-year-olds just get a bedtime.
The day says you can finally give in to your sweet tooth and eat as much candy as you want. Official permission to raid the Halloween bucket.

It honors Dr. Marthenia "Tina" Dupree, known as "The Chicken Lady," who spent 12 years as Director of Community Relations and Training at one of the world's largest chicken restaurants. A cluck-ing good career.
The first Easy-Bake Oven, from Kenner in 1963, baked with an ordinary light bulb. Light bulb moment, indeed.
The first doughnuts in America were little "nuts" of dough, brought over by the Pilgrims, who learned to make them in Holland. Pilgrims came for freedom, stayed for the dough.
Men who don't usually cook make dinner while everyone else stays out of the kitchen and just eats, stepping in only for an emergency. A smoke detector counts as an emergency.
Stephanie and Adrienne Vendetti, founders of the website How to be a Redhead, created it to remind women of every hair color to love who they are. Even brunettes are invited.
It began in 2011 after Bank of America announced a $5 monthly debit card fee, and about 40,000 people joined credit unions that day. Five dollars can start a revolution.
The old American Football League of the 1960s came up with the scoreboard clock, two-point conversions and names on jerseys. Now we know who to cheer for.
Basketball began with peach baskets nailed ten feet up at a YMCA gym, nine players per team, and a soccer ball. Nobody was dunking on a peach basket.

Nachos trace to 1943, when the wives of ten U.S. soldiers from Fort Duncan, Texas, stopped at Club Victoria in Piedras Negras, Mexico, where the chef was Ignacio "Nacho." Dinner plans turned into snack history.
The saxophone's inventor, Adolphe Sax, was born in Belgium in 1814 and played clarinet and flute before moving to Paris in 1842 to start an instrument business. Smooth move, Adolphe.
Some folks celebrate by purposely getting lost and finding their way back without a compass. Your phone's map is cheating.
Created in 2001 by a Fort Lauderdale attorney, it bans lawyer jokes and lawyer bashing for the day. Objection overruled, no jokes today.
The teddy bear is named after President Theodore Roosevelt, who was pictured in a famous 1902 cartoon refusing to shoot a bear. Best press a bear ever got.
In 1973 a New Jersey ruling made it the first state to allow girls in Little League, a year after 11-year-old Marcia Pepe of Hoboken played three games. Play ball, indeed.
Reading sharpens the mind, reduces stress and makes readers more empathetic. Not bad for something you can do in your pajamas.
The word "notary" comes from "nota," a shorthand developed by Cicero's clerk to take down Cicero's speeches. Some stamps of approval go way back.
